stem: Match each AWS monitoring or audit service on the left with the question it is best suited to answer on the right.

right.text: Which IAM user invoked a specific Bedrock model, and at what time?
Has the invocation latency of a SageMaker endpoint increased in the last hour?
Has the statistical distribution of incoming inference data drifted from the training baseline?
Which input feature most influenced a specific loan-denial prediction?

explanation.why_correct: CloudTrail answers 'who did what, and when' questions such as which principal invoked a model (R1). CloudWatch answers operational health questions such as latency trends (R2). SageMaker Model Monitor answers data-drift questions by comparing live inference data to a training baseline (R3).
explanation.rule_of_thumb: CloudTrail = API call audit trail. CloudWatch = operational metrics/alarms. Model Monitor = drift detection against a baseline. Feature attribution (R4) belongs to SageMaker Clarify, not any of these three.

stem: Match each governance/compliance scenario on the left with the AWS capability best suited to address it on the right.

left.text: Auditors need proof of exactly which principal invoked a Bedrock model and when, over the past quarter
The security team wants a real-time alarm if a SageMaker endpoint's inference latency spikes
The ML team wants to know if production traffic has statistically drifted from the training data distribution

explanation.why_correct: An audit of who invoked a model and when is answered by CloudTrail's API call history (R1). A real-time latency spike alarm is a CloudWatch alarm on an operational metric (R2). Detecting that production data has drifted from the training distribution is exactly what SageMaker Model Monitor is built for (R3).
explanation.rule_of_thumb: CloudTrail = who/when audit trail. CloudWatch = live operational metrics and alarms. Model Monitor = drift detection against a training baseline. SageMaker Clarify (R4) is for bias/explainability, not audit, alarms, or drift.
